name: Jeshaiah
overview: Jeshaiah was a male Levite, specifically a descendant of Merari, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. He is noted in Scripture for being sent to Ezra, highlighting his role within the Levitical community during the return from exile. His identity is closely tied to his tribal affiliation and Levitical heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshaiah means 'YHWH will save,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that underscores God's saving power. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 8:19 and was not given directly by God but carries a clear declaration of divine salvation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jeshaiah as a descendant of Merari, linking him to one of the principal Levitical families. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshaiah's significance lies in his role as a Levite sent to Ezra, which indicates his participation in the religious and communal restoration led by Ezra after the Babylonian exile. Being a descendant of Merari situates him within the Levitical order responsible for specific duties in the worship and service of God. His mention underscores the careful organization and leadership among the returned exiles, emphasizing the faithfulness to God's appointed structures.
